arxiv-1804-01717.title: Application of Symmetry Groups to the Observability Analysis of Partial Differential Equations
arxiv-1804-01717.creator: Bernd Kolar, Hubert Rams, Markus Schöberl
arxiv-1804-01717.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Bernd Kolar, Hubert Rams, Markus Schöberl. Symmetry groups of PDEs allow to transform solutions continuously into other solutions. In this paper, we use this property for the observability analysis of nonlinear PDEs with input and output. Based on a differential-geometric representation of the nonlinear system, we derive conditions for the existence of special symmetry groups that do not change the trajectories of the input and the output.

arxiv-2308-14847.title: NSF: Neural Surface Fields for Human Modeling from Monocular Depth
arxiv-2308-14847.creator: Yuxuan Xue, Bharat Lal Bhatnagar, Riccardo Marin, Nikolaos Sarafianos, Yuanlu Xu, Gerard Pons-Moll, Tony Tung, [0.4ex] Tübingen AI Center
arxiv-2308-14847.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuxuan Xue, Bharat Lal Bhatnagar, Riccardo Marin, Nikolaos Sarafianos, Yuanlu Xu, Gerard Pons-Moll, Tony Tung, [0.4ex] Tübingen AI Center. Obtaining personalized 3D animatable avatars from a monocular camera has several real world applications in gaming, virtual try-on, animation, and VR/XR, etc. However, it is very challenging to model dynamic and fine-grained clothing deformations from such sparse data. Existing methods for modeling 3D humans from depth data have limitations in terms of computational efficiency, mesh coherency, and flexibility in resolution and topology.

arxiv-2312-07114.title: STM in the fractional quantum Hall effect: Spectroscopy of composite-fermion bound states
arxiv-2312-07114.creator: Mytraya Gattu 1 , G. J. Sreejith 2 , and J. K. Jain 1
arxiv-2312-07114.description: Abstract The fractional quantum Hall states are non-Fermi liquids of electrons, in that their ground states and low energy excitations are described not in terms of electrons but in terms of composite fermions which are bound states of electrons and 2 ​ p 2p quantized vortices.

arxiv-2409-02965.title: Do We Trust What They Say or What They Do? A Multimodal User Embedding Provides Personalized Explanations
arxiv-2409-02965.creator: Zhicheng Ren, Zhiping Xiao, Yizhou Sun
arxiv-2409-02965.description: Abstract With the rapid development of social media, the importance of analyzing social network user data has also been put on the agenda. User representation learning in social media is a critical area of research, based on which we can conduct personalized content delivery, or detect malicious actors.

arxiv-2507-13515.title: Evolutionary Period Changes for 25 X-ray Binaries and the Measurement of an Empirical Universal Law for Angular Momentum Loss in Accreting Binaries Facilities: AAVSO, DASCH, TESS, ZTF, MAST
arxiv-2507-13515.creator: Bradley E. Schaefer
arxiv-2507-13515.description: Abstract I measure and collect timings of phase markers (like eclipse times) for the orbits of 25 X-ray binaries (XRBs) so as to calculate the steady evolutionary period change ( P ˙ \dot{P} ). I combine these with my observed P ˙ \dot{P} measures from 52 cataclysmic variables (CVs).

arxiv-2508-04794.title: Automorphism gadgets in homological product codes
arxiv-2508-04794.creator: Noah Berthusen, Michael J. Gullans, Yifan Hong, Maryam Mudassar, Shi Jie Samuel Tan
arxiv-2508-04794.description: Abstract The homological product is a general-purpose recipe that forges new quantum codes from arbitrary classical or quantum input codes, often providing enhanced error-correcting properties. When the input codes are classical linear codes, it is also known as the hypergraph product. We investigate structured homological product codes that admit logical operations arising from permutation symmetries in their input codes.

arxiv-2509-25291.title: Mathematical Framework for Epidemic Dynamics: Optimal Control and Global Sensitivity Analysis
arxiv-2509-25291.creator: Liban Ismail, Yahyeh Souleiman, Saralees Nadarajah, Abdisalam Hassan
arxiv-2509-25291.description: Abstract This study develops and analyzes an extended Susceptible–Infected–Hospitalized–Recovered (SIHR) model incorporating time-dependent control functions to capture preventive measures (e.g., distancing, mask use) and resource-limited therapeutic interventions. This formulation provides a realistic mathematical framework for modeling public health responses beyond classical uncontrolled epidemic models.

arxiv-2602-14970.title: Counterfactual Fairness Evaluation of LLM-Based Contact Center Agent Quality Assurance System
arxiv-2602-14970.creator: Kawin Mayilvaghanan, Siddhant Gupta, Ayush Kumar
arxiv-2602-14970.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in contact-center Quality Assurance (QA) to automate agent performance evaluation and coaching feedback. While LLMs offer unprecedented scalability and speed, their reliance on web-scale training data raises concerns regarding demographic and behavioral biases that may distort workforce assessment.

pmc-11433046.title: Research Interest in Copper Materials for Caries Management: A Bibliometric Analysis
pmc-11433046.creator: Veena Wenqing Xu, Mohammed Zahedul Islam Nizami, Iris Xiaoxue Yin, John Yun Niu, Ollie Yiru Yu, Chun-Hung Chu, Regina Maria Puppin-Rontani
pmc-11433046.description: This study examined research interest in copper materials for caries management. We conducted an exhaustive literature search of English publications on copper materials for caries management. We removed duplicate publications and screened the titles and abstracts to identify relevant publications. Then, we analyzed the bibliometric data of the publications using the Bibliometrix and VOSviewer programs.

pmc-11511067.title: Dynamic Spatial-Temporal Memory Augmentation Network for Traffic Prediction
pmc-11511067.creator: Huibing Zhang, Qianxin Xie, Zhaoyu Shou, Yunhao Gao, Shyan-Ming Yuan
pmc-11511067.description: Traffic flow prediction plays a crucial role in the development of smart cities. However, existing studies face challenges in effectively capturing spatio-temporal contexts, handling hierarchical temporal features, and understanding spatial heterogeneity. To better manage the spatio-temporal correlations inherent in traffic flow, we present a novel model called Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Memory-Augmented Network (DSTMAN).

pmc-12666647.title: Home sputum collection for Aspergillus fumigatus detection in adults with cystic fibrosis
pmc-12666647.creator: Gina Hong, Joanna Walsh, Allen Koshy, Jesse Y. Hsu, Anna L. O'Dea, Elisa M. Vesely, Warda Memon, Rebecca H. Dezube, Christopher H. Goss, Louisa B. Goss, Alicia Greene, Jane E. Gross, Alexandra Wilson, David P. Nichols, Sean X. Zhang, Robert A. Cramer
pmc-12666647.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundElexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) has impacted the ability for people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF) to spontaneously expectorate sputum, leading to lower respiratory sampling rates and infection detection challenges. Home sampling may permit a potential strategy for fungal detection in PwCF.MethodsWe conducted a prospective decentralised cohort study of PwCF to test the feasibility of home sputum collection and ambient temperature transport for Aspergillus fumigatus (Af) detection. Participants collected and shipped weekly sputum samples from home to the laboratory for fungal culture and completed electronic questionnaires.

pmc-12784842.title: The Impact of Nanoplastics on the Quality of Fish Sperm: A Review
pmc-12784842.creator: Hayam Djafar, Saira Naz, Maria Montserrat Rivera Del Alamo, Juan Carlos Balasch, Mariana Teles
pmc-12784842.description: Simple SummaryNanoplastics (NPs) are increasingly present in aquatic environments and are small enough to interact directly with biological cells. Fish sperm are particularly vulnerable because they are released directly into the water during fertilization and have limited protective and repair mechanisms.

pmc-12859553.title: A pathogen peptidoglycan scaffold coated with artificial biomembrane promotes broad resistance to bacterial infections by dynamically reprogramming macrophage metabolism
pmc-12859553.creator: Junjie Guo, Shuo Jia, Zibo Mai, Chaonan Wang, Zheng Jia, Jiaqing Wang, Xinran Yao, Jiaqi Liu, Fang Wang, Junwei Ge
pmc-12859553.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The increasing severity of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria and the shortage of effective treatment strategies urgently require the development of new immunotherapies to combat superbug infections. Trained immunity may offer a novel and effective mechanism to combat resistant superbugs. However, there are currently few materials capable of effectively activating trained immunity, highlighting the need for new agents that provide more durable protection.

pmc-13021511.title: A framework for estimating manure nitrogen balance and recycling potential for current and future conditions in the USA
pmc-13021511.creator: Yanyu Wang, Xin Zhang, Sheri Spiegal, Eric A Davidson
pmc-13021511.description: Manure recycling can ameliorate pollution and fertilizer demand, but varying assumptions about recoverable manure nutrients and crop requirements complicate understanding of manure recycling potential. Using nitrogen (N) in the contiguous USA as a case study, we applied methods from six studies to compare manure N balance estimates (recoverable manure minus crop demand).

pmc-13209120.title: Development and Field Construction Protection of a Fiber Bragg Grating-Geogrid Integrated System in Asphalt Pavements
pmc-13209120.creator: Hui Wang, Da Zhang, Qiaoyi Li, Guangqing Yang, Peng Xu, Xunmei Liang
pmc-13209120.description: Facing the challenges in field monitoring of the mechanical response of geogrids in asphalt pavements, this study integrated two types of Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors, unarmored and armored, into geogrids using the pillar-stitching technique on industrial warp-knitting production lines.

pmc-13355368.title: Reinforced double-layer vein patch angioplasty in carotid endarterectomy to mitigate patch aneurysm
pmc-13355368.creator: Aidin Baghbani, Luis Guilarte, Quang Le, Shah-Jahan M Dodwad, S Keisin Wang
pmc-13355368.description: Carotid endarterectomy with patch angioplasty is standard for symptomatic carotid stenosis. However, prosthetic patches carry a risk of infection, particularly in patients with recent endocarditis. We report the case of a 67-year-old man who presented with central retinal artery occlusion and active mitral valve vegetation and subsequently underwent left carotid endarterectomy using a dual-layer facial vein patch.

pmc-13429582.title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of developing mouse hearts reveals a spatially patterned signaling environment
pmc-13429582.creator: Junqi Hu, Haoting He, Juan Xu, William A. MacDonald, Yuanhang He, Tianhao Liu, Wei Chen, Guang Li
pmc-13429582.description: Heart development involves dynamic signaling interactions between cells and their surrounding environment (niche). Single-cell mRNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has been widely used to profile gene expression in individual cells, but it faces challenges in dissecting niche signals due to the need for cell dissociation. In contrast, spatial transcriptomics can preserve tissue structure and represents a potentially effective approach for this purpose.
